history.dynasty: Paramara (11th-12th c.); later upkeep by Maratha/Holkar patrons
history.summary: Ancient stone temple on the banks of the Kshipra, about 6 km from the Mahakaleshwar Temple and 7 km from Ujjain railway station on the Fatehabad road. The swayambhu (self-manifested) Ganesha idol is flanked by Riddhi and Siddhi; one account describes the deity in three forms - Chintaman (remover of worries), Ichhaman (fulfiller of desires) and Siddhivinayak (giver of riddhi-siddhi). The assembly hall's finely carved stone pillars reflect the Paramara period; the shrine complex also has idols of Shiva, Parvati, Vishnu and Saraswati. Later rulers including Ahilyabai Holkar contributed to upkeep. This is a separate ancient temple, distinct from Bade Ganeshji Ka Mandir (seq 563) near Mahakaleshwar. The CSV gives no address beyond Ujjain, MP (no town/state error); coordinates are approximate - the geocoder did not return the temple as a distinct POI (verify on the ground).

name: Chintaman Ganesh Temple
town_description: Ancient city on the Shipra (Kshipra) River in Madhya Pradesh, one of Hinduism's seven Sapta Puri, home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga and the Simhastha Kumbh Mela held every 12 years.
